reranked_evidence.title: Will raise voice in Parliament for loco pilots: Rahul Gandhi
reranked_evidence.snippet: ## The Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha on Sunday flagged the plight of loco pilots who are "deprived of basic facilities like urinals, have no limit on working hours and neither do they get leaves". Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Sunday flagged the plight of loco pilots and asserted that the INDIA bloc will raise its voice in Parliament to improve their rights and working conditions. Gandhi's remarks on X came as he posted a video of his recent interaction with loco pilots at the New Delhi Railway Station. The Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance (INDIA) will raise its voice in Parliament to improve the rights and working conditions of loco pilots, Gandhi asserted. R Kumaresan, who played a crucial role in organising the interaction between the former Congress president and the loco pilots at the New Delhi Railway Station on Friday, told PTI that they wanted to bring to Gandhi's attention "serious safety issues" faced by drivers and passengers in the Railways.

reranked_evidence.title: Shri Rahul Gandhi meets railways loco pilots, they complain of inadequate rest
reranked_evidence.snippet: * In Focus* Voice of the Nation. ##### Shri Rahul Gandhi meets railways loco pilots, they complain of inadequate rest. New Delhi: Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on July 5, 2024, met a group of Indian Railways loco pilots, who complained of “inadequate rest due to understaffing”. Shri Rahul Gandhi assured them that he would raise their issues in Parliament. He met more than 50 loco pilots from all over India at the New Delhi railway station and they explained to him their issues. Basically, the loco pilots complained of inadequate rest, they said. The lack of rest is caused by understaffing due to the government halting recruitment of loco pilots, the Party sources claimed. Leader of Opposition Shri Rahul Gandhi assured the loco pilots that he has been consistently raising the issue of “railways’ privatisation and lack of recruitment”, the sources said, adding that the Congress leader listened to their concerns and supported their demand for adequate rest.
